correctness.rationale: All n>=2 are covered by a self-contained proof. On the unrestricted de Bruijn graph, mandatory 00-free n-windows create unit deficit at each boundary 1...0 vertex and unit surplus at each boundary 0...1 vertex. In any completion, one flow path leaves each source, and cannot reach any positive sink before shifting away the source’s complete initial 1-run; total extra cost is at least E_{n-1}. Explicit append-one paths biject sources to sinks in exactly those lengths without forbidden edges; the resulting strongly connected balanced multigraph admits an Euler tour. A Fibonacci recurrence proves E_{n-1}=F_n-1 and hence length L_{n+1}-1. The verified standard-library generator checks construction, windows, and n=2..12, plus exhaustive absence of shorter cycles at n<=5; an independently implemented min-cost flow solver agrees for n<=12. The finite computations are supplementary and do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The Fibonacci language is the canonical binary finite-type constraint. Its shortest cyclic universal covering sequence, including boundary-incompatible yet linearly admissible windows, is a natural exact design invariant. The nonbalanced graph forces a strictly positive and exponentially increasing number of repeats for n>=3; the theorem evaluates it sharply for every n and gives a constructive Eulerian repair. The result distinguishes cyclically forbidden de Bruijn cycles from all-linear-window coverage and can support constrained indexing/test-sequence constructions. No unsupported application performance gain is claimed.
